metaData.title: BestBlogs Subscription Source Sharing: First Wave – WeChat Official Accounts
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article is the first installment of the BestBlogs subscription source curation series, systematically sharing 375 carefully selected WeChat Official Account RSS feeds covering nine major fields including AI, software programming, and investment & finance, along with an OPML file for import.
metaData.summary: This article is the first installment of the BestBlogs subscription source curation and sharing series, focusing on WeChat Official Accounts. The author has compiled 375 actively updated WeChat Official Account RSS feeds, categorized according to BestBlogs' nine major classification system (Artificial Intelligence, Investment & Finance, Business & Technology, Software Programming, Lifestyle & Culture, Media & News, Personal Growth, Product Design, Sports). Each source includes its name, priority, description, and recommendation rationale. The article explains why WeChat Official Accounts were prioritized (they host a wealth of high-quality Chinese original content but are difficult to manage) and the value of RSS (transforming platform content into subscribable, portable, open sources). It also provides a download link for the OPML file and hints at future sharing of lists for X/Twitter, podcasts, and other sources. Overall, this is a high-quality information source curation checklist rather than an in-depth analytical piece.

mainPoints.point: BestBlogs has curated 375 high-quality WeChat Official Account RSS feeds, covering nine major fields.
mainPoints.explanation: These sources have been vetted, organized by categories such as AI, Investment & Finance, and Business & Technology, and include priority levels and recommendation reasons to help readers build high-quality information intake channels.

mainPoints.point: RSS is an effective solution to the scattered and hard-to-manage nature of WeChat Official Account content.
mainPoints.explanation: RSS transforms platform-bound content into subscribable, importable, and portable open sources, allowing readers to manage their information flow autonomously rather than passively accepting platform recommendations.

mainPoints.point: BestBlogs' core principle is 'users choose sources first, then AI helps filter'.
mainPoints.explanation: This contrasts with black-box recommendation feeds, emphasizing the reader's active choice. It involves first deciding on long-term sources and directions, then leveraging AI to reduce the cost of filtering.

keyQuotes: First find sources worth following long-term, then let AI help filter, sort, and understand.

relatedArticles.title: BestBlogs Weekly Issue 86: Infrastructure
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This weekly delves into the evolution of AI infrastructure, covering everything from AlphaGo's general reasoning methods to Claude Code's six-layer engineering architecture, emphasizing that with the popularization of AI programming, architectural judgment, engineering constraints, and personal memory are becoming new core competencies.

relatedArticles.title: Orange: The Internet is Dead, Long Live the Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth exploration of the paradigm shift from the Internet's stock era to the AI Agent's incremental era, proposing the logic of "Agent-native" product and organizational transformation.

relatedArticles.title: Tech Enthusiast Weekly (Issue 389): How to Hire Programmers in the Future
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This issue explores the paradigm shift in programmer hiring in the AI era and aggregates cutting-edge technical trends and developer tools, including infrared communication, rack-mounted hydroponics, and Meilisearch.

relatedArticles.title: BestBlogs 2.0 Internal Beta Launch: I Want to Rebuild a Reading Product That Better Suits Myself
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article is the author's in-depth retrospective on the upgrade of their personal project BestBlogs to version 2.0, explaining the product philosophy shift from 'content aggregation' to a 'reading workflow', aiming to solve the problems of discovering, judging, and efficiently reading high-quality content in the era of information overload.

relatedArticles.title: Yu Yi: How to Efficiently Manage 100 Agents to Work for You
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Explores the management mindset of transforming from an AI user to an 'AI Chairman,' achieving efficient collaboration for a 100-Agent team through asynchronous communication, tiered decision-making, and compounding engineering.

relatedArticles.title: BestBlogs Weekly Issue #87: Self-Evolution
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: With 'Self-Evolution' as the core theme, this issue provides an in-depth analysis of the latest advancements in autonomous AI model iteration, the reshaping of programming toolchains, and edge inference infrastructure, while exploring the paradigm shift of the developer's role from coder to conductor in the AI era.

relatedArticles.title: This AI Hotspot Website, Encapsulating 3 Years of My Self-Media Experience, Is Now Free for Everyone.
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The author publicly shares his AI hotspot monitoring website, AIHOT, and details its information curation architecture and iterative experience, which combines source filtering, AI scoring, and code-based rules.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores how coding agents are shifting the software development bottleneck from 'implementation' to 'review,' redefining the collaboration models and core competencies of Engineering, Product, and Design (EPD) teams.

relatedArticles.title: 20 Hidden Gem Skills Worth Recommending: Niche but Surprisingly Useful
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article curates and details 20 Claude Skills tailored for Chinese content creators, covering writing, image generation, research, productivity tools, and entrepreneurial development, along with installation commands and usage tips.

relatedArticles.title: BestBlogs Weekly Issue 91: Infrastructure Week
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This week's issue, themed 'Infrastructure Week', provides an in-depth analysis of the evolution of the complete technology stack in the AI agent field, from models and execution layers to infrastructure. It focuses on key developments such as Cloudflare Agent Week, Claude Opus 4.7, Codex upgrades, and the Hermes open-source project, extracting the core insight that the industry is shifting from demos to production-grade systems, with engineering discipline and governance mechanisms becoming the core competitive advantages.
